In this section we are going to look at graph traversal.
Now graph traversal means that we are visiting all nodes of the graph.
Now let's say we have a graph like this.
Now the question is if we start from vertex A in which direction we will go, are we going to visit
first B or we are going to visit C.
And which node will come after for example B or C.
So to be able to decide the order of the visits in the node, we have two types of graph traversal algorithms
breadth first search and depth first search.
Now we are going to look at them separately.
So let's concentrate on the first one which is breadth first search.
Now breadth first search.
In short, we can say BFS is an algorithm for traversing the graph data structure.
And it starts at some arbitrary node of the graph and explores the neighbor nodes first before moving
to the next level.
So what does it mean?
So in this graph, if you start from the vertex A, we know that the neighbors of vertex A are b, C,
and d.
So this means that after visiting A it's going to continue to the neighbors.
So the first neighbor is B it's going to visit B, then it will continue to the next neighbor which
is going to be C.
Then it will continue to the next neighbor which is D.
So after exploring the old neighbors, it will come to the first neighbor and explore its neighbors.
So in this case the first neighbor is B, and it will come over here and explore the unvisited unvisited
vertices of this node, which is E in this case.
So as you can see, if we start from a, the order is like this.
We are visiting first A, then explore the neighbor nodes, then continue to the first neighbor node
and explore its neighbor nodes.
And it continues like this until we finish the all unvisited nodes.
So the logic is very simple.
